newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Minister sees budget cuts under CZK20bln-CTK.
newsitem.headline: Czech Minister sees budget cuts under CZK20bln-CTK.

text.p: The Czech government is expected to propose a package of state budget cuts of just under 20 billion crowns, Health Minister Jan Strasky told the Czech news agency CTK on Monday.
"Closely under, but this is not the last word," Strasky said in answering a question whether the cuts would total 20 billion crowns.
Strasky was on his way to a government meeting where the cuts were expected to be finalised.
He added there are still to be discussions on some price liberalisations and pensions which will affect the final extent of the cuts.
The government faces a confidence vote in parliament this week which will determine the future of embattled Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus and his economic programme.

Klaus's three-party, centre-right coalition controls only 100 seats in the 200-seat lower house and even members of the government have been driving hard bargains for their support in the vote, which could come as early as Tuesday.

Coalition leaders met earlier on Monday and the full government is currently meeting to hammer out the budget cuts that form part of an austerity programme one party wants adopted in exchange for its support.
Deputy Prime Minister Josef Lux's Christian Democratic Union (KDU-CSL) has said it wants the programme, agreed by coalition leaders late last month, adopted by the government.
The Christian Democrats also want measures to deregulate rents and energy prices, agreed in March, postponed.
The KDU-CSL and Michal Zantovsky's Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA) are insisting on a balanced budget but Klaus has said the differences were not insurmountable.
